summary: The note explains the technology that underpins Esports events, contrasting digital arenas with traditional sports venues. It covers screens, broadcasting, networking, power and cooling, player equipment, audience interactivity, security, sustainability and technology integration, using named venues and events as examples. It argues that these arenas are as important to the experience as the games themselves.
one_line: An overview of the broadcasting, networking, cooling, security and sustainability technology that powers Esports arenas compared with traditional sports venues.
key_facts: The 'Global Esports Federation Summit' on September 5, 2023 highlighted that Esports tournaments now attract millions of simultaneous viewers worldwide.

Jane Thompson, CTO of Cybervenue, was the summit's keynote speaker and said, "Our goal is to construct not just stages or venues but universes within which our digital athletes and their fans can thrive."
Cybervenue is described as a leading Esports arena design company.
The Neon Clash venue opened in Austin on October 12, 2023, with a central stage with 360-degree screens giving every audience member an unobstructed view.
Neon Clash has a dedicated broadcast center with cameras, audio systems and mixing capabilities for streaming high-definition video to platforms like Twitch and YouTube.
The 'Allied Esports Network', launching November 14, 2023, has laid groundwork for a mesh of fiberoptic connections so interactions occur in near real-time.
Derrick Liu, a network engineer for the Allied Esports Network project, said, "It’s about perfecting the unseen."
The Esports Arena Dallas, unveiled January 5, 2024, uses a state-of-the-art liquid cooling setup to manage heat from servers and computing devices.
Esports Hub Los Angeles debuted in February 2024 with stations featuring adjustable desks, chairs and ambient lighting.
Unlike standardized equipment in traditional sports, Esports players often use peripherals they are comfortable with.
The 'Digital Fortress' Esports event on March 20, 2024 used biometric access for players, DDoS mitigation systems and real-time network monitoring.
SolarCore Arena, set to open in Miami in late 2024, is designed to be eco-friendly with solar panels, kinetic floor tiles and sustainable materials.
Esports arenas offer audience interactivity such as VR stations and participation segments, which have no direct counterpart in traditional sporting venues.
